Main text in two-line-indented verse in italic, then a woodcut ornament and a section heading CHI POPVLI SV-pra claustra Caspia, then a paragraph of roman text with marginal citation "Valer. Arg. lib.5." in the left margin, ending with catchword "Cum" at the lower right.

p.i: Mossonychi vos & stabulis Macrones ab altis,
Byzeresque vagi, Philyræq;, à nomine dicta
Litora, quæ cornu pepulit Saturnus equino.
Vltimus inde sinus, sæuúmque cubile Promethei
Cernitur, in gelidas consurgens Caucasus Arctos.
Nec prosunt Scythiæ sua frigora. Caucasus ardet.
— nec me latuere fluentes
Arboribus succi, sunestarúmque potestas
Herbarum, quidquid lethali germine pollens
Caucasus, & Scythicæ vernant in gramine rupes.
— & te vel per Alpium iuga,
Inhospitalem & Caucasum,
Vel Occidentis vsque ad vltimum sinum,
Forti sequemur pectore.
Ipsæ Caucaseo steriles in vertice sylvæ,
Quas animosi Euri assidue frangúntq;, serúntque,
Dant alios alia fœtus: dant utile lignum
Nauigiis pinos, domibus cedrósque cupressosque.
Hinc radios truere rotis, hinc tympana planstris
Agricola, & pandas ratibus posuere carinas
Viminibus salices fœcunda, frondibus ulmi.

main_text.head: COLCHI POPVLI SVpra claustra Caspia.
main_text.p: Valer.Arg. lib.5.IXerat hæc, patriúmq; viam detorquet ad amne, Sacráque terrifica supplex mouet irrita noctì. Ille autem incœptum, famula duce, protinus vrget Aëre septus iter: patitur nec regia cerni Iuno virum, prior Æetæ ne nuntius assit. Iámque inerat populo, mediaque incognitus vrbi, Cum

page.notes: Woodcut ornament above the heading. The opening capital "D" of the paragraph is a large woodcut initial, the first word read as "Ixerat" with the initial D. Several marginal note texts are partly faded and uncertain; the left-margin notes are transcribed as best read. Verse lines are set in italic type.
